facts.current: helpful for processing emotions and feeling less alone in grief
a safe space to share their story, listen to others without fear of judgment, and express emotions
sense of community and facilitator guidance

plans.text: Gather all items that remind them of their grandmother and organize them in a way that feels right, while considering adding photos and mementos from other family members
Set small goals and track progress by starting with 10–15 minutes a day, three times a week
Start reading "Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Crest Trail" by Cheryl Strayed
Check out "Daring Greatly" by Brené Brown
Seek out a therapist or counselor who can provide guidance and support
Consider joining online forums or social media communities focused on grief, loss, and mental health
Start a journal to process emotions and reflect on experiences
Reach out to friends and family members who have gone through similar experiences

superseded_plans.text: Gather grandmother's belongings, photos, and other mementos to create a memory box for reflection
